findings.reason: the node should route the `--root` seed through the existing additive mechanism or hoist its existence filter, rather than re-deriving the same query, which the plan's otherwise citation-heavy §14 does not mention.
findings.text: the plan's seed-fix node proposes making `seed_facility_roots` "create only the rows that do not exist and leave an existing row's status, depth, scores and timestamps as they are", but `seed_missing_roots` in the same file already performs exactly this: it queries `MATCH (p:FacilityPath {facility_id}) WHERE p.path IN $paths RETURN p.path`, diffs to `missing_paths`, and delegates to `seed_facility_roots`, so the additive semantics the node plans to invent already exist one function below the one it will edit; `--add-roots` (paths.py:236) already reaches them

findings.reason: extend the owner (share one existence filter; retire the now-redundant wrapper) instead of forking it, so the two cannot drift on a facility-scoped path query.
findings.text: the existence check `existing_paths = {r["path"] for r in result}` / `missing_paths = [...]` at frontier.py:625-628 is the sole owner of "which roots already exist", and §14's seed-fix makes `seed_facility_roots` re-implement it, leaving two filters for one invariant (and making `seed_missing_roots` a redundant pre-filter once the seed is additive); the census of this pattern in the discovery package is one existing instance (frontier.py:625) plus the proposed one
